key_insight: Single-matrix SVD compression is locally optimal, but better LLM compression comes from optimizing across three scopes: matrix, block, and full-model loss.
engineering_relevance: For practical LLM deployment, the work shows that block-level joint optimization can markedly improve perplexity at a given compression ratio, especially when calibration data are limited.
method: L1: whitened SVD truncation on each matrix.
L2: joint optimization over Transformer blocks to correct compounding errors.
L3: end-to-end language-modeling loss refinement using 256 calibration sequences.
evidence_signal: On LLaMA-7B at 60% compression, WikiText-2 perplexity improved from 42.1 to 19.1 to 11.4 across the three stages, with gains reported across 20-80% compression and multiple architectures.
watch_item: The gains are strongest under a specific offline calibration setup; cross-architecture and ratio-sweep results use different protocols, and downstream task accuracy remains far below the dense model.
paper_title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression
